# Persisted decimal coercions: independent base catalog

`legacy_decimal_catalog_63a964a82f.json` contains protobuf `TableDef` values
generated by the real CREATE TABLE planner at
`63a964a82fbaae4759cfabb45655e0185bc0979c`, before the integer-to-decimal
declared-precision checks in PR #30639. JSON encodes each protobuf as base64.
These are not obsolete casts injected into freshly bound head plans.

The fixture keys correspond to these complete statements:

```sql
-- signed_compare
create table legacy_cmp(i bigint, tm time(0), constraint ck check(i > tm));
-- unsigned_compare
create table legacy_cmp(i bigint unsigned, tm time(0), constraint ck check(i > tm));
-- bit_compare
create table legacy_cmp(i bit(64), tm time(0), constraint ck check(i > tm));
-- arithmetic
create table legacy_cmp(i bigint, tm time(0), constraint ck check(abs(i + tm) > 0));
-- fractional_arithmetic
create table legacy_cmp(i bigint, tm time(6), constraint ck check(abs(i + tm) > 0));
-- explicit_decimal
create table legacy_cmp(i bigint, tm time(0), constraint ck check(cast(i as decimal(18,0)) > tm));
-- generated_compare
create table legacy_cmp(i bigint, tm time(0), g bool generated always as (i > tm) stored);
-- nested_explicit
create table legacy_cmp(i bigint, tm time(0), constraint ck check(cast(abs(i + tm) as decimal(18,0)) > 0));
-- declared_assignment
create table legacy_cmp(i bigint, tm time(0), g decimal(18,0) generated always as (i) stored);
-- ranged_compare
create table legacy_cmp(i bigint, tm time(0), constraint ck check(i not between tm and tm));
```

To regenerate, use an isolated checkout at the exact base and build its native
dependencies with `make cgo`. In a temporary package-plan test, iterate the SQL
above using `parsers.ParseOne(ctx, dialect.MYSQL, sql, 1)` and
`BuildPlan(NewMockCompilerContext(false, newPlanTestProcess(t)), stmt, false)`.
Marshal `p.GetDdl().GetCreateTable().GetTableDef()` with its protobuf `Marshal`
method and serialize the resulting `map[string][]byte` with
`json.MarshalIndent(fixtures, "", "  ")`. Free each parsed statement.
Do not regenerate with the new binder or fabricate its expression trees.

At the base, the signed, unsigned and BIT comparison expressions were also
executed at `10^18-1` and `10^18` with TIME zero; all six controls returned true.
On the unnormalized new reader, the same stored expressions reject `10^18`.
The head tests unmarshal these bytes and exercise the real expression executor,
both catalog resolver entry points, fresh-binding equivalence, copy-on-write,
idempotence, and unchanged declared-assignment/explicit-CAST contracts.
The fractional arithmetic fixture uses a small lower control because the old
scale conversion already overflowed physically for larger inputs.

This is an old-writer/new-reader component regression, not a claim of a live
server rolling-upgrade or binary-restart test.

`legacy_decimal_between_63a964a82f.json` is generated at that same exact base
with the same parser/planner/protobuf procedure. It adds genuine three-argument
BETWEEN (the earlier NOT BETWEEN fixture lowers to binary comparisons):

```sql
-- generated_between
create table legacy_cmp(i bigint, tm time(0), g bool generated always as
  (i between cast('00:00:00' as time(0)) and cast('00:00:01' as time(0))) stored);
-- explicit_between
create table legacy_cmp(i bigint, tm time(0), g bool generated always as
  (cast(i as decimal(18,0)) between cast('00:00:00' as time(0))
   and cast('00:00:01' as time(0))) stored);
```

The generator verifies the persisted function is `between` with three arguments.
On the base, the implicit fixture executes both `10^18-1` and `10^18` as false.
The new reader regression retains those exact serialized bytes, verifies the
unmigrated failure, compares the migrated predicate with fresh binding across
the signed domain and both interval endpoints, and preserves the explicit CAST.

`legacy_decimal_in_range_63a964a82f.json` uses the same exact-base procedure
for the four-argument numeric interval function. The generator checks the
function name and arity, and executes each persisted predicate at `10^18-1`,
`10^18`, and `MaxInt64` on the old writer; all return false.

```sql
-- generated_in_range_0 through generated_in_range_3:
-- repeat with the final flag 0, 1, 2, and 3, respectively.
create table legacy_cmp(i bigint, tm time(0), g bool generated always as
  (in_range(i,cast('00:00:00' as time(0)),cast('00:00:01' as time(0)),0)) stored);
-- explicit_in_range
create table legacy_cmp(i bigint, tm time(0), g bool generated always as
  (in_range(cast(i as decimal(18,0)),cast('00:00:00' as time(0)),
            cast('00:00:01' as time(0)),0)) stored);
```

The new-reader tests prove the implicit Decimal64(18,0) failure before migration
and Decimal128(19,0) recovery afterward, full signed-domain and fresh-binding
equivalence, all four open/closed endpoint modes, NULL propagation, unchanged
explicit CAST behavior, catalog immutability, and idempotence. The fourth
argument is a UINT8 boundary flag, not a numeric operand to widen.
